summary: Server exposes sensitive information via headers like X-Content-Type-Options.

remediation.code_diff:
--- a/handlers/router.go
+++ b/handlers/router.go
@@ -58,10 +58,13 @@
 	return s.middleware(mux)
 }
 
-// middleware adds permissive CORS and recovers panics with a verbose page.
-// VULN: security-headers no Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options or Referrer-Policy are ever set
+// middleware sets baseline security headers, adds CORS and recovers panics.
 func (s *Server) middleware(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
 	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+		w.Header().Set("Content-Security-Policy", "default-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'")
+		w.Header().Set("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")
+		w.Header().Set("X-Frame-Options", "DENY")
+		w.Header().Set("Referrer-Policy", "no-referrer")
 		w.Header().Set("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*") // VULN: cors-misconfig wildcard origin combined with credentials
 		w.Header().Set("Access-Control-Allow-Credentials", "true")
 		w.Header().Set("Access-Control-Allow-Headers", "Authorization, Content-Type")
remediation.config_change: Set Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY (or frame-ancestors), Referrer-Policy: no-referrer and, over TLS, Strict-Transport-Security on every response in shared middleware or at the reverse proxy.
remediation.virtual_patch:
SecRule &RESPONSE_HEADERS:Content-Security-Policy "@eq 0" "id:9100012,phase:3,pass,log,t:none,msg:'assay security-headers virtual patch f-be983aea8cbfd46f',tag:'assay/security-headers'"
{"class":"security-headers","engine":"modsecurity","finding":"f-be983aea8cbfd46f","id":9100012,"rule":"SecRule \u0026RESPONSE_HEADERS:Content-Security-Policy \"@eq 0\" \"id:9100012,phase:3,pass,log,t:none,msg:'assay security-headers virtual patch f-be983aea8cbfd46f',tag:'assay/security-headers'\""}

summary: Using a non-standard username bypasses the login mechanism.

validation.note: anonymous baseline is not consistently denied

remediation.config_change: Trace the authentication decision for POST /login to a single server-side check that cannot be influenced by client input; invalidate sessions created through the bypass; add a regression test.
remediation.virtual_patch:
SecRule REQUEST_URI "@rx ^/login" "id:9100006,phase:2,pass,log,t:none,msg:'assay auth-bypass virtual patch f-1a7b0ca6776bf67c',tag:'assay/auth-bypass'"
{"class":"auth-bypass","engine":"modsecurity","finding":"f-1a7b0ca6776bf67c","id":9100006,"rule":"SecRule REQUEST_URI \"@rx ^/login\" \"id:9100006,phase:2,pass,log,t:none,msg:'assay auth-bypass virtual patch f-1a7b0ca6776bf67c',tag:'assay/auth-bypass'\""}

validation.note: ground truth does not mark this path as requiring authentication

remediation.config_change: Require an authenticated session (and the appropriate role) on GET /; register the check in shared middleware so new routes inherit it; return 401 without credentials and 403 for the wrong role.
remediation.virtual_patch:

summary: The application allows injection via the `username` and `password` parameters which are reflected back in the HTML.

remediation.config_change: HTML-escape <parameter> before writing it into the page for POST /login.php (html/template or the framework's auto-escaping renderer); send Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8 and a Content-Security-Policy without 'unsafe-inline'.

summary: The application allows CSRF attacks due to the presence of a hidden form field (`user_token`) and the lack of proper token validation.

validation.note: post forms carry a token or the session cookie is SameSite

remediation.config_change: Require a per-session anti-CSRF token on state-changing requests to /login.php; reject GET for state changes; set SameSite=Lax or Strict on the session cookie and verify Origin/Referer.
remediation.virtual_patch:
SecRule REQUEST_METHOD "@rx ^(?:POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE)$" "id:9100019,phase:2,pass,log,t:none,msg:'assay csrf virtual patch f-d94537b7b5b23f52',tag:'assay/csrf'"
{"class":"csrf","engine":"modsecurity","finding":"f-d94537b7b5b23f52","id":9100019,"rule":"SecRule REQUEST_METHOD \"@rx ^(?:POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE)$\" \"id:9100019,phase:2,pass,log,t:none,msg:'assay csrf virtual patch f-d94537b7b5b23f52',tag:'assay/csrf'\""}

summary: The application stores user input and renders it in feedback without proper sanitization, allowing for XSS attacks.

remediation.config_change: Escape <parameter> at render time wherever it is displayed (not only at POST /); if rich text is required, sanitize with an allowlist HTML sanitizer at write time and store the sanitized form; add a Content-Security-Policy.
